Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' counter-wrestling system in eight volumes (about 7 hours): how a jiu-jitsu player beats wrestlers by using the front headlock and attacking the turtle. Volumes 1 and 2 cover foundations of the front headlock and getting it from standing and from top (down block, knee cut). Volume 3 covers the 4-point position (seated anaconda, anaconda throws). Volumes 4 and 5 cover the turtle and front headlock submissions (anaconda variations, the cross jump). Volume 6 covers the rear body lock (kosoto trips). Volume 7 covers maintaining 4-point and mat returns. Volume 8 covers back attacks and finishing the rear naked choke on the strong and weak sides.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi grapplers who struggle against wrestlers, or who want a front headlock and turtle attack game.
key: Front headlock from standing and top
Rear body lock and mat returns

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' no-gi closed guard in four volumes (about 3 hours). Volume 1 is mindset and the hand fight (don't wait, win the arms). Volume 2 is the closed guard armbar, dealing with the stack, and finishing the armbar from top. Volume 3 covers posture breaks, threatening to stand up and pendulum movement. Volume 4 covers the arm-across guard and its armbar, the pendulum sweep and related attacks.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi players who want an active closed guard rather than a stalling one.
key: Armbar and dealing with the stack

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones on getting back to your feet instead of accepting bottom positions, in four volumes (about 3.5 hours). He argues that many traditional pins and controls are weak against someone who simply prioritises standing up. He shows how to stand up from turtle, seated guard and bottom positions, using wrestle-ups and stand-ups, and how to hold down explosive opponents who are trying to do the same to you. The publisher listing has no per-volume breakdown.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi competitors, especially under rule sets that reward getting up.
key: Standing up from turtle and bottom positions
Holding down people who try to stand

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' updated Z guard (knee shield half guard) course in six volumes (about 5 hours). Volume 1 covers positioning and retention. Volume 2 covers the passes people use against Z guard and how to counter each (hip switch and others). Volume 3 covers kimura attacks (and kimura to armbar). Volume 4 covers the choi bar and building an armbar. Volume 5 covers the K guard back take, single leg X entries and the 'sweep first, submit second' idea. Volume 6 covers transitions against kneeling and standing opponents.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi half guard players who use a knee shield.
key: K guard back take and SLX entries

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: A single 46-minute video on Craig Jones' 'pendejo guard', a seated or half-guard style position he uses to enter leg locks (it is used with the false reap entry). It shows how to get to the position and the leg lock entries from it. No publisher chapter list was found.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi leg lockers who already know the basics.
sources: Based on the title and Craig Jones' related False Reap Accusations course.

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' original octopus guard course in three volumes (about 85 minutes). From bottom side control or half guard, you reach around the opponent's back to come up and create scrambles. Volume 1 covers beating the crossface and the step-over. Volume 2 covers kosoto sweeps, the kosoto hip bump and the height scramble. Volume 3 covers the 'octopus buggy', the buggy darce and digging out of deep holes.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Anyone who gets pinned under pressure passers; works for any body type.

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' early Z guard course in three volumes (about 2 hours), from around the time of his breakout ADCC 2017 run. It covers his knee shield half guard, the sweeps and back takes from it, and leg lock entries. Marked 'outdated' in your collection; Make Z Guard Great Again is the newer version. The publisher listing has no per-volume breakdown.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Craig Jones fans; the newer course is a better starting point.

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: The follow-up to Down Under Leg Attacks (about 3.5 hours) in four volumes. Volume 1 covers finishing the inside heel hook from the saddle. Volume 2 covers the 'hidden heel' problem and 50/50 attacks (exposing the heel). Volumes 3 and 4 are mostly live rolls, then Craig's narrated commentary on those rolls.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Leg lockers who want to see the techniques applied in live rolling.

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' original leg lock system (about 2.5 hours, four volumes), the one he used in his breakout ADCC 2017 run. It covers his main heel hook entries and finishes from the saddle, outside ashi and 50/50, and his Z guard / half guard leg entries. Marked 'outdated' in your collection since later courses refined it. The publisher listing has no per-volume breakdown.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Historical interest and fundamentals of Craig's leg locks.

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones on the false reap, a leg lock entry that crosses your leg over in a way that looks like (but isn't) an illegal reap under IBJJF-style rules. Four volumes (about 2 hours) show how to use it from popular no-gi guards like the Z guard and pendejo guard to enter heel hooks. The publisher listing has no per-volume breakdown.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi leg lockers looking for a reliable entry.
key: Entries from Z guard and pendejo guard

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones combines triangles and leg locks into a dilemma system across eight volumes (about 7 hours). Volume 1 covers leg lock breaking mechanics. Volume 2 covers straight locks (ankle lock, 50/50 straight ankle, kneebars). Volume 3 covers triangle finishing mechanics (front triangle and others). Volume 4 covers entering the triangle from bottom (fighting for 2-on-1 grips). Volume 5 covers entering from top with the shoulder pry. Volume 6 covers the dilemma itself, switching from the triangle to the legs (front triangle to backside 50/50). Volume 7 covers ashi garami off-balancing and entering reverse X. Volume 8 is commentary on matches against Jake Shields, Vinny Magalhães, Gilbert Burns and others.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Intermediate-advanced no-gi players who want submissions that feed each other.
key: Switching between triangle and leg attacks

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: An early, single-video (36-minute) Craig Jones course on setting up and finishing the triangle. Marked 'outdated' since Systematic Submission Dilemmas covers triangles in much more depth.

Craig Jones' kneebar course in four volumes (about 2.5 hours): kneebar entries from top (passing, the leg drag and back step) and bottom positions, and the finishing details that make the kneebar work against resisting opponents. The publisher listing has no per-volume breakdown.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Leg lockers who want the kneebar as a finish when the heel hook isn't available.
key: Kneebar entries from top and bottom

Craig Jones- Octopus Guard 2.0.overview: Craig Jones' updated octopus guard in four volumes (31 short files, about 2h 45m). It refines the original reach-around guard with cleaner entries, stronger off-balancing and smoother transitions to the back, to the legs and to top position. The files are numbered by volume and lesson (e.g. 7484256256098-2-3 = volume 2, lesson 3) and the publisher listing doesn't break down individual lessons.
Craig Jones- Octopus Guard 2.0.for: Anyone stuck under pressure passers; the newer version of the octopus guard.
key: Transitions to the back, legs and top
